candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the raw, unsmoothed $close driving the numerator, adding day-to-day noise/turnover to an otherwise strong, saturated ratio (fitness 10.336). Working memory already exhausted window-resize (5-day: 0.898 corr), mean-substitution, and high/low-removal mutations of this exact family, so none of those are repeated here. Instead this wraps only the numerator's price reference in a light 3-day EMA, denoising the fastest-moving input while leaving both 21-day range bounds untouched. Because EMA is a time-series smooth (not a per-day monotonic transform of the final ratio), it genuinely reshapes cross-sectional ordering over time rather than just replicating the parent's rank correlation the way a top-level rank/zscore wrapper would.

This 2-node tree has only one real component to target: the field, currently used as a static level. A static quarterly-stamped ROA level is highly persistent and largely anticipated by the market; the missing piece is any time dimension. Swapping to a ~1-quarter (63-day) change captures fundamentals improving vs deteriorating (a fundamental-momentum signal) instead of a stale level. Level and delta are not monotonic transforms of one another, so correlation with the parent should drop meaningfully rather than trivially matching it.

This is the only one of the four parents with zero cross-sectional normalization: raw dollar volume spans orders of magnitude across the panel, so a 21-day mean of raw levels is dominated by permanent size effects rather than genuine relative-liquidity information (consistent with its being the weakest-fitness parent, 2.168). Inserting RANK inside the average, ranking each day before averaging 21 daily ranks, fixes this without touching the field or window. Rank-then-average is not equivalent to average-then-rank (they don't commute), so this changes the induced ordering rather than being a no-op monotonic wrapper on the finished output.

This is last round's only acceptance per working memory, so the validated 3-day decayed-return term and the operating_margin field choice (explicitly favored over roe/accrual) are both left untouched. The weaker element is CS_ZSCORE on a margin ratio, which can be skewed by a handful of extreme or near-zero-denominator outliers that then dominate the interaction's magnitude. Swapping to CS_RANK keeps the same reversal-x-quality interaction but makes the fundamental term bounded and outlier-robust.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.
